sources_considered.why: Contemporary primary account by Google's robotics research head identifies unresolved mechanical and intelligence challenges and explains the limits of narrow robot programming.
Primary evaluation documents real progress in language-guided kitchen tasks and provides necessary counterweight to an overly broad reading.
Archived AI Day captions discuss humanoid intelligence limits, but transcription quality and the archive's publication date were not sufficiently established.
The primary event page did not supply the relevant transcript through read_page.

evidence_items.locator: Section “Making sense of our worlds,” first paragraph
evidence_items.explanation: Google's robotics research head describes unresolved real-world adaptation and understanding, with helpful robots still limited to restricted kitchen tasks and explicit safety controls. Applying these shared robotics limitations to general household humanoids is an inference, rather than a direct humanoid safety test.

evidence_items.locator: Section “Performance on Temporally-Extended, Complex, and Abstract Instructions,” caption following the results table
evidence_items.explanation: This is material evidence of progress in interpreting and planning household-like requests. It concerns a restricted kitchen evaluation on a different robot platform, so it does not establish safe, general-purpose humanoid household operation.

unresolved_gaps: The reviewed evidence does not provide a comprehensive, standardized safety evaluation of every humanoid available in 2022.
The distance implied by “well beyond” cannot be quantified from the wording or the cited evaluations.
